top_signal.title: I’m struggling to understand the “free work for portfolio” strategy. Does it actually lead to paying clients?
top_signal.summary: I run a small business myself, and lately I keep seeing people in web design/development actively advertising free websites because they need portfolio projects.   I’ve seen it on Reddit, TikTok and Instagram, including paid ads offering websites for free, and I’m honestly struggling to understand the business logic behind it.   I completely understand doing one or two projects for friends, helping an NGO, or deliberately taking on something unpaid because the experience is valuable. I’ve done extra work myself without charging for every single thing when I wanted to learn or strengthen my portfolio.   What I don’t really understand is turning “free” into the actual acquisition strategy.   If one person offers a website for free and another asks €1,000, maybe the buyer thinks €500 sounds reasonable. But if several people repeatedly offer similar work for free, I wonder how you later convince the same market that the service is worth €100, €200, €500 or €1,000.   That’s the part that concerns me, especially because I also see plenty of posts a few months later from freelancers saying they can’t find paying clients or that nobody values web work anymore.   I’m not saying every unpaid project is bad, and I’m definitely not writing this from a position where clients are lining up at my door.
